samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore` re-implements `readOnlyDocStore`'s Proxy trap logic line-for-line instead of reusing a shared helper — and the two copies have already diverged
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:118-185 duplicates packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:67-169 almost verbatim: same memoization map, same non-configurable/non-writable `get` exception, same set/defineProperty/deleteProperty/getPrototypeOf/setPrototypeOf/preventExtensions/isExtensible/has/getOwnPropertyDescriptor/ownKeys traps, same `batch(fn)` special case; only the reader allowlist and two extras (HISTORY_METHODS, the READ_ONLY_VIEWS idempotence WeakSet) differ. Both are documented as access-control boundaries, so a trap fix in one silently misses the other — divergence is already present (notes is idempotent and returns null from undo/redo; docs is neither). The generic part belongs in `@wafflebase/core`, which packages/docs already depends on.

samples.summary: The claim this change declares wrong ("the wrapper is the write boundary on a default install") is left standing in the docs package, so the repo now documents two contradictory answers
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:57-70 and docs/design/notes/notes.md ("What that wrapper is not") record that reasoning as wrong, but packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:39-42 still says "with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one", and packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413 repeats the same shadow-mode framing.

samples.summary: Backend webhook changes (boot-time posture log, document key/verb in the shadow-deny log) are a different subsystem from the share-link notes parity issue this branch is scoped to
samples.evidence: The cited issue (#1044, per shared-notes-layout.tsx:30 and docs/design/notes/notes.md) is notes share-link toolbar/upload parity. `logPosture()` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:118-140) and the new `target=` field in the shadow log change backend observability for all document types. Disclosed in docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md's Risks section, so not hidden — but unrequested scope riding along with a frontend parity change.

samples.summary: New Risks bullet credits revision history with asserting `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true` itself; no such runtime assertion exists
samples.evidence: The mitigation says "features whose safety depends on the distinction (the public template tier, revision history) assert `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true` themselves". True for the template tier (register-templates.ts:154, template-review.ts:80, template.service.ts:470); for revision history the only occurrence is a test harness setting the env var (packages/backend/test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:292). A doc crediting a safeguard the code lacks is worse than silence.

samples.summary: The mobile `both`→`edit` demotion rule is now copy-pasted across two routes rather than shared
samples.evidence: shared-notes-layout.tsx:56-62 reproduces notes-detail.tsx:112-120 (same expression and rationale comment), and both must stay in sync with notes-toolbar.tsx:399-403's `visibleModes` filter — the toolbar comment in this diff had to be edited precisely because the rule now lives in two mounts. A shared hook (or letting the toolbar own the demotion) would keep it in one place.

samples.summary: The previously recorded reason the share route did not pass `showAuthors` (a bundle-chunking constraint from importing `notes-settings`) is now violated and the doc update never retires it
samples.evidence: The comment deleted from shared-document.tsx said passing `showAuthors` "would mean importing `notes-settings` into this route too, which makes Rollup hoist it — and the notes engine with it — into a shared chunk well past the chunk-size gate". shared-notes-layout.tsx:7-11 imports `notes-settings` and NotesView statically and shared-document.tsx:35 imports the layout statically, i.e. exactly the graph that rationale ruled out. Chunk budgets are CI-enforced so the code may be fine; the gap is that neither the doc nor the new module records why the old constraint no longer holds.

samples.summary: Divider geometry change (7px → 25px hit area, `touch-action`, ratio-track fix) is an engine-wide visual change beyond the share-link parity issue
samples.evidence: editor.ts:286-302 plus the pointer-move `track` change (~line 535) alter the split divider for every notes mount including desktop. Documented in notes.md ("The divider was fixed in the engine rather than per route") and plausibly part of the mobile-split complaint, but it is a separate concern from toolbar/upload parity.

verdict.reason: The duplication is present exactly as described. packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:93-185 reproduces packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:67-169 near-verbatim: identical memoization Map with {raw, view} entries (notes:98 / docs:71), identical non-configurable+non-writable `get` exception (notes:112-115 / docs:84-87), identical non-function hide (notes:117 / docs:96), identical cache check (notes:119-120 / docs:98-99), identical `batch(fn)` runner (notes:127-136 / docs:104-112), and traps set/defineProperty/deleteProperty/getPrototypeOf/setPrototypeOf/preventExtensions/isExtensible/has/getOwnPropertyDescriptor/ownKeys with the same predicates and even the same comment text (notes:149-180 / docs:122-167). The only deltas are the ones the finding names: the reader allowlists (notes:19-27 vs docs:21-30), HISTORY_METHODS/noHistory returning null (notes:35,100,125-126), and the READ_ONLY_VIEWS idempotence WeakSet (notes:43,94,183) — docs has neither, so divergence is already real. The reuse target also checks out: packages/docs/package.json:56 depends on @wafflebase/core and packages/core exists. I looked for grounds to refute and found none that hold: docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md:46-48 makes "Store abstraction unification" a Non-Goal, but that is about a common base interface for DocStore/Store/SlidesStore bound to their model types, not about a generic Proxy-trap helper; and its own risk mitigation (241-243) gates Tier C/D "until a concrete second consumer exists", which notes now is. docs/design/notes/notes.md:289-304 documents the sibling relationship deliberately, but a doc endorsing a copy does not prevent the copies diverging. Both headers (docs:44-65, notes:69-91) describe the traps as an access-control boundary, so a trap fix in one silently misses the other — the rubric's major bullet for duplicated logic that will diverge and give two answers to the same question.
